title: Sadre Alam v. Ajay Kumar Gautam, EE — further time to comply with Clause 6.5 consideration direction
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Prima facie civil contempt of a Clause 6.5 consideration direction found; Executive Engineer given six further weeks to comply; contempt application disposed of with liberty to apply afresh on continued default. Disputed assessment not examined.
headnote: Where a writ had already directed the Executive Engineer to consider a Clause 6.5 representation against a disputed assessment within a fixed time, alleged non-compliance was treated as prima facie civil contempt. The High Court granted one more six-week opportunity to comply and disposed of the contempt application with liberty to move afresh if default continued, without examining the bill.
facts: The applicant, a consumer, had in Writ C No. 6882 of 2020 been relegated to a Clause 6.5 representation against a disputed assessment, with a direction that if he applied within two weeks the Executive Engineer would consider and dispose of it within six weeks. He says he submitted a certified copy on 12 March 2020 and the Executive Engineer wilfully failed to comply. He sought punishment under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

holding_units.holding: A civil contempt alleging that the Executive Engineer failed to consider a Clause 6.5 representation, as already directed by the writ court, does not reopen the disputed assessment. Where a prima facie case of non-compliance is made out, the Court may grant a further time-bound opportunity to dispose of the 6.5 representation in accordance with law and close the contempt with liberty to apply afresh on continued default.

principle_tags.application: The Court enforced the earlier 6.5 consideration direction by granting further time and did not examine or redecide the disputed assessment.
The underlying writ had confined the consumer to a Clause 6.5 representation against the disputed assessment; this contempt only polices compliance with that statutory forum.

not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the bill or other allied issues under Clause 6.5.
Only a prima facie case was recorded; one more opportunity to comply was granted and the application was disposed of at this stage.
